correctness.rationale: Each host gives a closed walk of the same length in the directed admissible overlap graph, recording its classes on successive edges. Conversely a closed walk gives the periodic host spelled by the edge symbols; overlap and closure enforce all windows, including for walks shorter than the window length. The bit-mask BFS finds a shortest return to its start with all classes visited. Independently, python3 /workspace/branches/independent_finite.py circles (NumPy integer arrays) exhausts both versions for lengths at most 28: extend all linearly legal words one symbol at a time, discard exactly those with a forbidden wrap, and test modular windows against separate oriented and reversal masks. The oriented and reversal minima, respectively, are (3,6,10,17,28) and (3,6,10,17,23) for orders 2–6. The specified 23-symbol witness was directly checked. The extra order-one comparison in the reproduction ties, with minima 2 in both versions. There is no extrapolation beyond order six.

value.rationale: This is the first strict gain in a natural run-length-limited cyclic covering problem, not an isolated example. Knowing that four smaller orders admit no gain and that the first saving is exactly five positions gives a sharp benchmark for constrained reversal-cover constructions: counting reversal classes alone significantly underestimates the optimum. This finite comparison is useful without an all-order formula.
